info.name: CCE Receiver Adaptor
info.description:
OpenMRS CCE Receiver Adaptor API — receives FHIR R4 payloads and routes them to OpenMRS via FHIR or REST endpoints based on CapabilityStatement discovery.

Base URL: http://localhost:8083

## Routing
- **FHIR path**: Patient, Encounter, Observation, Condition, Location, Practitioner, Medication, AllergyIntolerance, Immunization, Task, Group, DiagnosticReport, Person
- **REST fallback**: ServiceRequest → TestOrder, MedicationRequest → DrugOrder, RelatedPerson, OperationDefinition

## OpenMRS-Specific Notes
- **Patient**: Our adaptor auto-enriches with OpenMRS ID (Luhn Mod 30) + identifier location extension. No need to include these manually.
- **Encounter**: Must NOT include `participant` array (causes ConstraintViolationException). Encounter datetime must be in the past.
- **Observation**: `code.coding[0].code` must be an OpenMRS concept UUID (e.g. 5085AAAA... for Systolic). LOINC/SNOMED codes won't resolve unless the concept has a matching source mapping.
- **ServiceRequest**: Requires `requester` (maps to orderer). Routed via REST as TestOrder.
- **MedicationRequest**: Requires OpenMRS drug order configuration (order.drugDosingUnitsConceptUuid etc.) to be set. Not functional on unconfigured instances.
- **Sub-elements**: FHIR element `id` fields must be present (UUID format) on array sub-elements like `name[]`, `identifier[]`, `address[]`, `telecom[]`. Our adaptor auto-adds these.

## Test Reference Data (from demo OpenMRS)
- Patient: b4b2e0a1-7ef8-4fea-acd7-19dd3c40a189
- Encounter: 7eccfa30-7e6b-43a5-8e89-e8a4d423ecc8
- Location: b1a8b05e-3542-4037-bbd3-998ee9c40574 (Inpatient Ward)
- Provider: f9badd80-ab76-11e2-9e96-0800200c9a66 (Super User)
- Encounter Type: e22e39fd-7db2-45e7-80f1-60fa0d5a4378 (Admission)
- Concepts: 5085AAAA...AA (Systolic), 5089AAAA...AA (Weight), 5088AAAA...AA (Temperature)
- Drug: 57232ace-ba38-4cc6-b817-ba4f55e645d5 (Aspirin 100mg)

item.name: FHIR Resource API
item.description: Main inbound endpoint for receiving FHIR R4 payloads. Each request is routed to OpenMRS via FHIR or REST based on CapabilityStatement.

request.description:
Creates a Patient in OpenMRS via FHIR. The adaptor auto-enriches with:
- OpenMRS ID (Luhn Mod 30 check digit)
- Identifier location extension
- UUID `id` fields on name/address/telecom/identifier sub-elements

No OpenMRS-specific fields needed in the request.

Creates an Encounter in OpenMRS via FHIR.

**OpenMRS-specific requirements:**
- `type[0].coding[0].code` must be a valid OpenMRS encounter type UUID
- Do NOT include `participant` array (causes ConstraintViolationException in FHIR module v1.2.2)
- `period.start` must be in the past (OpenMRS validates encounterDatetime < now)
- `status` should be `unknown` (OpenMRS default)
- `subject` must reference an existing Patient

Creates an Observation (vital sign) in OpenMRS via FHIR.

**OpenMRS-specific requirements:**
- `code.coding[0].code` MUST be an OpenMRS concept UUID (e.g. 5085AAAA...AA for Systolic). Standard LOINC codes (e.g. 8480-6) will NOT resolve to a concept and will fail with 'concept: Cannot be empty or null'.
- `subject` must reference an existing Patient
- `encounter` should reference an existing Encounter

**Common concept UUIDs:**
- Systolic: 5085AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA
- Diastolic: 5086AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA
- Temperature: 5088AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA
- Weight (kg): 5089AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA
- Height (cm): 5090AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA

Creates a ServiceRequest → TestOrder in OpenMRS via REST fallback.

**OpenMRS-specific requirements:**
- `requester` is REQUIRED — maps to `orderer` (provider UUID). Without it, OpenMRS returns a validation error (500 with serialization bug).
- `code.coding[0].code` must be a valid OpenMRS concept UUID
- `subject` and `encounter` must reference existing resources
- Maps to REST endpoint: POST /ws/rest/v1/order with type=testorder
- `careSetting` defaults to OUTPATIENT
- `intent` maps to action: 'order'→NEW, 'revoke'→DISCONTINUE

Creates a MedicationRequest → DrugOrder in OpenMRS via REST fallback.

**⚠️ REQUIRES OpenMRS CONFIGURATION:**
Drug orders require the following system settings to be configured in OpenMRS:
- `order.drugDosingUnitsConceptUuid` — concept set with valid dose units (mg, tablet, etc.)
- `order.drugDispensingUnitsConceptUuid` — concept set with valid dispensing units
- `order.drugRoutesConceptUuid` — concept set with valid routes (oral, IV, etc.)
- `order.durationUnitsConceptUuid` — concept set with valid duration units (days, weeks, etc.)

Without these configured, ALL drug order creations will fail with 500 (ValidationException masked by serialization bug).

**Additional requirements:**
- `requester` is REQUIRED (maps to orderer)
- `medicationCodeableConcept.coding[0].code` must be an OpenMRS Drug-class concept UUID
- A matching Drug entry must exist (or use `medicationReference`)
- Maps to REST endpoint: POST /ws/rest/v1/order with type=drugorder

Sends a FHIR transaction Bundle containing Patient + Encounter + Observation. The adaptor splits the bundle into individual resources, sorts by dependency order (Patient → Encounter → Observation), and routes each independently.

**Notes:**
- Each entry is routed independently; failures in one don't roll back others
- Resources are sorted by dependency order: Location → Practitioner → Patient → Encounter → Observation
- Use `request.method` (POST/PUT/DELETE) per entry
- Bundle cross-references (urn:uuid) are NOT resolved by the adaptor — use actual OpenMRS resource UUIDs

item.name: Diagnostics
item.description: Diagnostic endpoints for inspecting CapabilityStatement cache and routing table.

request.description: Returns the cached CapabilityStatement from OpenMRS FHIR endpoint, listing all supported resource types and their operations (read, create, update, delete, search-type).
Returns the routing table showing which resource types are routed via FHIR vs REST, and which operations each supports.
